StackType.rationale: PowerStackType.Counter. The sim has no StackType concept; Power.on_stack (powers.py:64-66) adds unconditionally, which is what PowerCmd.ModifyAmount does (PowerCmd.cs:236). Third-file citations, not hashed here.

AfterSideTurnEnd.issue: The removal condition is inverted from a side comparison into a hard-coded side. FlameBarrierPower.cs:26-32 removes the power whenever `base.Owner.Side != side` -- i.e. at the end of the turn belonging to the side the owner is NOT on, which for a player-held Flame Barrier is the enemy side's end and for an enemy-held one is the PLAYER side's end. The sim only implements on_enemy_side_end (powers.py:689), so an enemy holding Flame Barrier keeps it forever. DORMANT: the only ported applier is the Ironclad card (Flame Barrier is a player card, so the owner is always the player and the enemy-side-end leg is the right one). Named trigger: any monster or effect that puts Flame Barrier on an enemy -- at which point the sim needs an on_player_turn_end / after_player_turn_end leg exactly as ConstrictPower and DemisePower carry (powers.py:1441-1447, :4059-4065). Also note the sim uses _expire() where C# uses PowerCmd.Remove; Flame Barrier overrides no AfterRemoved so the observable matches. Third-file citations, not hashed here.

guards.rationale: powers.py:679-680 calls is_powered_attack(props) explicitly. This power gets the gate RIGHT where power/thorns and power/curl_up -- the same reflect-on-being-hit shape -- both drop it, which is what makes those two omissions omissions rather than a shared architectural absence.

guards.what: FlameBarrierPower.cs:22 dealer = base.Owner on the reflected damage
guards.rationale: powers.py:684-687 passes `dealer=self.owner` and DamageProps.NON_CARD_UNPOWERED (UNPOWERED alone -- blockable, matching C# omitting Unblockable). Contrast power/thorns, which drops the dealer.

guards.what: Flame Barrier fires even when the hit was fully blocked
guards.rationale: C# ignores the DamageResult entirely (`DamageResult _` at :18), so a fully blocked powered attack still burns; powers.py:671-687 likewise tests no amount. The sim's on_damage_received does fire at hp_lost == 0 (cmds.py:121-122 is unconditional on amount), so this holds.

guards.issue: Both sides hang the reflect on the AFTER-damage hook, so C# skips it when the hit killed the victim (CreatureCmd.cs:392) and so does the sim (cmds.py:121) -- faithful. But note the contrast with power/thorns, whose C# hook is BeforeDamageReceived and therefore fires on the killing blow: the two powers really do differ in the game, and the sim collapses both onto on_damage_received, which is right here and wrong there. Verdict `gap` only to carry that cross-reference at the same precedence as the thorns finding it explains; nothing in THIS unit's behaviour diverges on the killing blow. Third-file citations, not hashed here.
